question: Should the first-party Wear companion and atomic phone-plus-Wear Play upload ship together in the same Android release path?
rationale: The runtime architecture follows the approved phone-proxy boundary, but coupling the Wear artifact to every phone upload creates a durable product and release-operations policy that code correctness alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Ship Together After Fixes
options.body: Keep the integrated first-party companion and atomic upload, but require all identified validation, compatibility, security-scan, and exact-head proof gaps to be resolved first.

options.title: Stage Release Integration
options.body: Land the bounded phone/watch runtime separately and add mandatory Wear Play upload only after a live edit and rollback procedure are proven.

options.title: Defer First-Party Wear
options.body: Pause this branch and retain the protocol foundation without committing the Android release process to a Wear artifact yet.

recommendation.title: Ship Together After Fixes
recommendation.body: Keep the integrated first-party companion and atomic upload, but require all identified validation, compatibility, security-scan, and exact-head proof gaps to be resolved first.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current-main protocol and canonical phone-proxy product direction, so they are best positioned to decide whether runtime and release coupling ship together.
